hero.headline: Walk in already knowing who needs you — and what to reteach before the test.
hero.subhead: Most teacher dashboards are a scoreboard: a wall of averages that tells you how the class did, never what to do next. So the gaps stay invisible until the test — you find out a whole class never had distributing-a-negative down only after it costs them points. Veradic opens to a to-do list, not a scoreboard: the students who need you first, the concept the class is stuck on, and the reteach set already written — before the test gets there first.

flowSetup.title: Open to a to-do list, not a scoreboard
flowSetup.caption: "Needs you today" sits at the top across every course you teach — flagged work first, then overdue, then ungraded, in the order a human should handle them. You're not reading a grid of averages and guessing where to start; the morning's queue is already triaged, Algebra and Geometry in one list.

flowSetup.title: One click lands you on the exact student
flowSetup.caption: Tap a name and you're standing in their actual work — Maya Chen's photographed page, the AI's grade beside it, the few it flagged for your eyes. No course-to-roster-to-submission hunt; the item that needed you opens straight to the thing that needed deciding.

moment.eyebrow: The moment that sets it apart
moment.title: Seeing the problem and fixing it are the same click.
moment.body: Open Student Insights and the class is ranked by where it's stuck, not who scored what — "6 of 8 missed distributing a negative across parentheses," right at the top, with each student's status beside it. Every other tool stops here: it shows you the gap and leaves the fix to your Sunday. Veradic puts a Re-teach button on that row. One click opens a practice set already titled for exactly that concept — and the AI writes ten fresh problems on it, on the spot. The signal and the fix are the same motion.
moment.sell: Most tools show you a dashboard of what went wrong. This turns it into ten problems that fix it — in one click.

payoff.title: What a teacher gets back.
payoff.lead: Not another dashboard to babysit. Four things that change how a teaching day starts:

points.title: Walk in knowing what needs you
points.body: The morning opens to a triaged queue across every course — flagged, then overdue, then ungraded — instead of a wall of averages you have to decode before you can even start.

points.title: Catch a class-wide gap before the test
points.body: "6 of 8 missed distributing a negative" surfaces while you can still do something about it — not in the post-mortem after the unit test has already cost them the points.

points.title: No student quietly falling behind
points.body: Every student carries a status — struggling, on track, thriving, or no activity yet — so the kid who's slipping in silence is visible now, not at report-card time.

points.title: A teaching signal, not a gradebook
points.body: This is formative: it points you at what to reteach next, never a column of grades. The struggle read is for you to act on, not a score that follows a student around.

payoff.closing: Walk in knowing who needs you, catch the class-wide gap before the test, and turn it into a reteach set in one click — every kid seen, nobody slipping by quietly. That's the day this gives back.
